newsitem.title: ALBANIA: German evacuees in Albania in exchange of fire.
newsitem.headline: German evacuees in Albania in exchange of fire.

text.p: German troops sent in by helicopter to help evacuate Western residents fleeing unrest in Albania fired on unidentified gunmen who shot at the evacuees and their aircraft on Friday.

A diplomatic source said 105 people, mostly Germans and other European Union nationals, eventually left aboard five helicopters and were taken to Montenegro on Albania's northern border. One Albanian was slightly hurt in the fracas, he said.

The mass evacuation of foreigners from the Albanian capital has proved to be a dangerous undertaking. The United States suspended its operation after one of its helicopters came under fire from a surface-to-air missile and an Italian helicopter also came under fire.

Pictures from a Turkish television crew obtained by Reuters television showed German troops first hitting the ground when the gunmen opened fire from a van and then shooting back as evacuees were boarding the helicopters.
The television footage showed several of the evacuees cowering on the tarmac at an airfield near the capital. Some were praying.
The diplomatic source said the evacuees were taken to the Montenegran capital of Podgorica and would be flown on to Frankfurt.
Diplomatic sources said they had opted for evacuation by helicopter as it was proving too dangerous on Albanian roads among large numbers of uncontrolled gunmen.

In Washington, a defence official announced that the United States had suspended its military evacuation of Americans after a Marine Cobra helicopter reported being fired on by a missile from the ground.
Another Cobra came under small-arms fire and returned the fire, the official said. Neither U.S. aircraft was hit. Officials said 480 U.S. nationals had been evacuated before the suspension.
